heading: NRI FCNR Deposits: Avoiding Currency Conversion Tax Errors
tldr: An NRI recently received relief from a ₹3.41 crore income tax addition due to a tax officer's currency conversion error.
The officer mistakenly treated Japanese Yen deposits in an FCNR account as Indian Rupees.
The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) Jaipur ruled in favour of the NRI, deleting the unjustified tax demand.
This highlights the critical importance for NRIs to maintain meticulous documentation for all foreign currency transactions.
Proper records, including bank statements and remittance proofs, are essential to substantiate the source of funds and prevent such errors.
caption:
Imagine getting a huge tax bill by mistake! That's what happened to an NRI whose foreign currency deposits were wrongly called Indian Rupees by the tax department. Luckily, the mistake was fixed. This shows why keeping clear records of your money, especially if it's in foreign currency, is super important. Learn more about this case and why your documents matter.
